absent: Rule insertion, lookup, matching evaluation, and filterkey or buflen accounting beyond comparison, deletion, listing and conversion.
Full struct definitions, field offsets, numeric ABI values, and wire layout of audit_rule_data and netlink messages.
Synchronization for logging, backlog queues, session counter visibility, and prune thread lifecycle.
Audit message handler dispatch, capability checks for administration, and kauditd delivery guarantees.
Filesystem-notify group setup, parent lifecycle, and tree hash management outside removal paths.

findings.text: audit_compare_rule decides management-level equivalence of two filter rules. Equality is signaled by zero and difference by one. Header control, every populated field slot, and the complete syscall mask all participate; string, path, credential and scalar payload families each use their own equality notion.

Two rules match only when control header values agree, when each field slot agrees on discriminator and operator, and when every mask word agrees. Payload handling is chosen by discriminator: security label text and filter keys use lexical comparison, watch and tree locations and executable marks use stored pathname comparison, user and group families use identity equality, and remaining kinds use numeric comparison.

Observed rule state comprises control scalars for flags, persistent flags, list selector, action and field population, a field array whose entries carry a type tag plus operator plus tagged payload able to hold text, numeric, user or group forms, a fixed-length syscall mask, a variable-length size, optional filter-key text, optional watch, tree and executable attachments, and linkage for global membership and per-object membership.

audit_del_rule deletes the active entry equivalent to a caller description. It reports ENOENT when nothing matches and success otherwise. On success the entry leaves global and object-local membership, watch, tree and executable attachments are detached, counters for total rules and signals are adjusted based on list kind and signal relevance, and memory is reclaimed after a grace period.

The filter mutex excludes concurrent writers and protects blocking readers of the rule set. Deletion holds it from lookup through unlink, attachment detachment and counter updates; rule dumping holds it only while copying entries into a private queue, releasing before background transmission.

Global rule linkage allows RCU readers. Deletion unlinks through RCU-aware removal, waits for a grace period before touching object state, and defers final freeing through an RCU callback, all while holding the filter mutex against other writers.

Rule enumeration delivers one reply per active rule across every filter table followed by a terminating marker. Snapshot assembly runs under mutex protection into a request-private queue that records network scope and requester identity; a dedicated background thread then performs transmission so the requesting context cannot deadlock on its own send buffer. Allocation or thread-start failure cleans the private queue and reports the failure.

Kernel-to-wire rule translation preserves flags combined with list selector, action, field population and mask. Each slot contributes discriminator and encoded operator; security labels, watch and tree locations, filter keys and executable marks are packed consecutively into a trailing buffer with per-slot lengths accumulated, legacy unset login-identifier form may normalize to a canonical unset value, and other kinds carry numeric payload directly.
String packing copies source bytes without terminator at the current cursor, advances the cursor by the copied length, and returns that length so callers can accumulate total variable size.

Watch, tree and executable-mark objects expose pathname accessors used for comparison and serialization. When the corresponding tracking feature is unavailable, header fallbacks supply an inert empty string form that is never expected to be dereferenced for real teardown in the tree case.

Tree detachment runs under a dedicated spin lock. It unlinks the rule from the tree and clears the back-pointer; if the tree becomes rule-free and is not already retiring, it is marked retiring, detached from its root linkage, queued for pruning and a prune wakeup is issued.

Watch detachment unlinks the rule from its watch. When the watch holds no further rules, the parent is temporarily retained, the watch is unlinked and its references dropped, an empty parent mark is destroyed, and the temporary retention is released. Parent retention tolerates null.
Executable-mark detachment operates on the mark attached to the rule and delegates teardown to the filesystem-notify mark layer.

Netlink control input processes every message in a datagram under the control lock, dispatching each to the message handler and acknowledging when requested or on error. After unlocking, backlog beyond the configured limit wakes the logging daemon and briefly parks the sender uninterruptibly to exert back-pressure.

Subsystem bring-up initializes buffer caches, log queues, inode hash buckets and command serialization, registers per-namespace netlink handling, marks initialization complete, starts the logging daemon with failure treated as fatal, and emits an initialization record. Boot options select default enablement and backlog capacity, retaining safe defaults with diagnostics on unparsable input.

Each network namespace owns one audit netlink endpoint created at namespace init with input plus multicast bind and unbind handling, non-root reception allowed and a short send timeout; namespace exit releases it. Bind requires read capability and logs connect outcome, denying with EPERM otherwise; unbind logs disconnect.

Configuration-change, multicast membership, denied-path and generic formatted records are suppressed when auditing is disabled and otherwise bracketed between start and end helpers. Records carry operation, identity, terminal, session, list and result attributes suited to each event, with task context and session info added where shown.

Login identifier update is permission-gated: unset callers may assign without privilege, while reassignment from a set value needs control capability unless immutable or only-unset restrictions forbid it. Valid identifiers allocate a fresh increasing session number while skipping the reserved unset value; invalid identifiers clear the session. Old and new identifiers plus sessions and outcome are always logged.

Session allocation performs a single retry when the freshly allocated value collides with the reserved unset sentinel. Wider wrap-around, reuse and repeated-collision handling are not visible in the fragments.

Object-context logging emits a single combined label when fewer than two object label providers exist, otherwise a placeholder plus an auxiliary record holding per-provider labels. Per-provider conversion failure logs an unknown marker, unexpected errors raise diagnostics, and the returned status reflects failure if any provider failed.

Packet logging resolves bridge-encapsulated frames to their carried IP family, then records addresses, protocol and, for stream and datagram transports, port pairs for both IP families. Truncated headers report memory shortage while unknown or unsupported families report placeholder addresses with a protocol-support error.

When filesystem audit support is compiled out, watch and tree removal helpers trap instead of succeeding, mark removal is an inert no-op, and path accessors yield empty strings. Callers must therefore only reach watch or tree teardown when a real attachment can exist.

Visible ABI surface includes user, exclude and filesystem filter selectors, rule-list reply and completion signaling, configuration-change, login, kernel and listener event kinds, auxiliary object-context records, login-identifier immutability and only-unset controls with legacy handling, unset user and session sentinels, mask-length and filter-count dimensions, audit netlink family with group limit, and bridge plus IP protocol selectors.
